correctness.rationale: Let T(X)=(P₁XP₁+P₂XP₂)/2 for the two orthogonal row-complement projections and let a=(1−c²)/2. The restriction of H to either complement line has quadratic form a times the squared norm, so T(H)=a(I−H), and T(I−H)=(1−a)(I−H) since T(I)=I−H. This proves the exact law for all t≥1. The eigenvalues (1±c)/2 of H give G_t and the maximum first-step quotient (1+c)²/2; at c=0 every initial direction maximizes. The logarithmic derivative of G_t has positive denominator and numerator h_t=1+(2t−5)c+c²−(2t+1)c³. Its signs at 0 and 1 are opposite; uniqueness follows by factorization at t=1, strict monotonicity of h₂, and one sign change for t≥3. The positive increment 2c(1−c²) forces the root rightward. The root identity 2(t−1)c_t(1+c_t)(1−c_t)=(3c_t−1)(1+c_t²) excludes a limit below 1 and gives t(1−c_t)→1. Then the geometric factor tends to e⁻¹ and t times the prefactor tends to 1. The first-step quotient crosses one at √2−1, whereas each later expected residual is multiplied by (1+c²)/2<1. The boundary c=1 is used only by continuity, not admitted as a row geometry.
residual_risks: The argument is exact and does not depend on running the uploaded verifier. The loss is a squared mean-row residual in expectation, not a pathwise statement or Euclidean solution error.

originality.rationale: The fixed-geometry dynamics follow by evaluating a standard moment recursion, the 1/t rate is known generally, and the first-step scalar factor and numerical coherence threshold coincide exactly with earlier greedy Kaczmarz values. The supported distinct contribution is the all-start, all-coherence finite-horizon envelope for the IID residual observable, including its unique moving optimizer and sharp asymptotic constant. Neither the greedy theorem nor the inspected generalized rates or alternative two-row models give that result.

value.rationale: The worst system varies with the horizon even though each fixed two-row system converges geometrically. The unique angle and 1/e coefficient give a concrete sharp benchmark for general last-iterate residual guarantees. The exact law also explains why an expected initial residual increase can coexist with strictly contracting later residuals.
residual_risks: The 1/e value is not a universal benchmark constant for arbitrary row systems or other loss normalizations.
